title: GTM Engineer
description:
THE ROLE 

Growth owns the systems that power our go-to-market motion: our CRM, connected to enrichment, sales engagement, outbound agents, lifecycle, routing, visitor intelligence and paid, with GTM OS, our internal platform, tying them together. We are hiring a GTM Engineer to run that motion and build the agents and data layer it depends on.

Nash builds the autonomic logistics platform: a system that senses what is happening across a network, decides what to do about it and adjusts as the results come back, without waiting to be told. Our go-to-market should run the same way. A signal comes in, an agent decides what to do with it, the rep gets the account ready to work, and every outcome writes back so the next decision is better than the last.

Most of the pieces exist. GTM OS is in production, the agents run, the stack is connected. Your job is to turn them into one reliable engine that produces pipeline, hold it to a production bar, then decide what it does next.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- 
Build and run the AI agents that work across our GTM motion: account research, signal qualification, message construction, routing and reply handling, from design through evals, rollout and the monitoring that keeps them honest

- 
Build the infrastructure to run paid and ABM as one system: audiences generated from the CRM, campaigns launched and paused by rules you write, engagement flowing back into the agents, and spend tied to accounts worked and pipeline created

- 
Own the account context layer every agent and campaign is grounded in: entity resolution, evidence typing, freshness and provenance, and the segment, industry, region and product rules that define our market

- 
Build on GTM OS, our internal platform, and make what it can do available to sales and marketing inside the tools they already use

- 
Be the technical owner of our go-to-market systems, the CRM and everything connected to it, from the data model and routing logic to the integrations and automations that keep the whole stack current and consistent

- 
Own sending infrastructure and deliverability: domain strategy, warming, suppression and sender reputation across every program that sends

- 
Hold the production bar: evals, observability, permissions and auditability, so the system reports its own failures before a rep finds them

- 
Be measured on what the motion produces: reply and meeting rates, pipeline and revenue, cost per account worked. Agent reliability and data quality are how you get there

WHAT YOU'LL BRING 

- 
A go-to-market record: outbound, paid, ABM or lifecycle programs you ran, with the pipeline they produced and the systems you built to run them

- 
Software you shipped and kept running: a service, agent or pipeline in production that other people depended on, with something we can look at

- 
Outbound that scales and still reads like a person: sequences triggered by something that just changed for the buyer and tied to what we sell, reply rates to show for them, and the judgment to pull apart a message that is not landing

- 
Paid media fluency: you have run budgets and built audiences, and you know which decisions should stay with a person

- 
Hands-on experience applying AI to go-to-market systems: agents, LLM-based automation, MCP-style integrations, and the evals that tell you whether any of it works

- 
Fluency in Python or TypeScript, and daily work with Claude Code, Cursor or equivalent, with specific opinions about where the tooling fails

- 
Integration experience: you have built and debugged integrations through APIs and understand auth, rate limits, sync direction and failure modes

- 
Salesforce as a developer: the data model, the API, and Apex, or the track record to pick it up fast

- 
Data fluency: SQL, warehouse concepts, and the habit of tracing a data quality issue from source to destination

- 
You can turn a vague request into scoped work and explain the tradeoffs

HOW TO APPLY 

Send us your resume, links to things you have built and kept running (a repo, a live service, an agent, a sequence with its results), and a short note on the system or motion you are most proud of and why. If you would rather skip the cover letter, send a Loom walking us through a piece of work, or a Replit prototype of a GTM agent you would build for Nash. Both are very much encouraged.

Want to grab our attention and bypass the recruiting platform? Record a video introducing yourself at testimonials.nash.ai with code JOIN-NASH. Your application notifies us in Slack the moment it lands, and we get some much needed testing coverage on our latest Claude build :)

More about Nash 

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics. 

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us 

✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off
✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

title: Cloud Infrastructure Engineer - Digital Assets
description:
Optiver is building its Digital Assets trading capabilities and is looking for a Cloud Infrastructure Engineer. This role sits in the Global Cloud Platforms team and will report to the Global Head of Cloud Platforms.

You will help build the foundations for a new trading tenancy on Optiver’s existing cloud platform. With a mature hybrid cloud infrastructure already in place, this role allows you to optimize it for the unique operational and performance needs of digital assets trading. Your focus in this role will be on extending our cloud platform to meet the performance demands of a latency-sensitive, always-on trading environment.

You’ll be accountable for delivering a secure, performant, and robust infrastructure that directly supports trading outcomes - stability, latency, resilience, and safe change in the digital assets space. 

What you'll do 

- 
Design low-latency infrastructure using cloud primitives and optimized configurations.

- 
Own and enhance cloud infrastructure performance setups.

- 
Build and run high-throughput, resilient connectivity patterns for exchange integrations.

- 
Drive security hygiene both on and off cloud with secrets management, network segmentation and traffic isolation.

- 
Implement governance and best practices for shared cloud platform ensuring safe multi-tenant operation.

- 
Deliver infrastructure as code using Terraform and Terragrunt, following Optiver standards and workflows.

- 
Build and maintain CI/CD and automated testing for changes minimizing risk in always-on markets.

- 
Implement and enhance observability using CloudWatch, Prometheus, Grafana, and similar tools.

- 
Participate in operational ownership through incident response, post-incident improvement, and continuous hardening. 

Who you are 

- 
Demonstrated expertise in owning production infrastructure as an engineer (Platform, SRE, or Infrastructure engineering background).

- 
Deep cloud infrastructure knowledge, especially around VPC design, compute optimization, and performance networking features.

- 
Proven ability to write and maintain Terraform modules and operate IaC safely through reviews, testing, and deployment pipelines.

- 
Solid Linux fundamentals, including networking and systems performance tuning.

- 
Ability to program in at least one language (e.g., Python or Go) for tooling, automation, and integration work.

- 
Collaborative skills to work effectively with other team members and stakeholders. 

- 
Ability to communicate technical information to both technical & non-technical stakeholders.

- 
Ability to gauge business problems and prioritize tasks accordingly.

Strong preference will be given to candidates with:

- 
Experience managing multi-cloud (AWS, GCP, AliCloud, etc) infrastructure.

- 
Experience building & managing latency-sensitive systems in cloud (trading, real-time systems, market data, etc.).

- 
Hands-on experience managing WebSocket infrastructure under burst load and unstable upstream conditions.

- 
Solid understanding of exchange rate limits / quota models (including weight-based limits) and how to engineer systems to respect them without compromising trading performance.

- 
Familiarity with high-performance networking concepts (e.g., SR-IOV , kernel/network tuning, exposure to RDMA / DPDK is a plus). 

Who we are 

At Optiver, our mission is to constantly improve the market by injecting liquidity, providing accurate pricing, increasing transparency and acting as a stabilizing force no matter the market conditions. With a focus on continuous improvement, we participate in the safeguarding of healthy and efficient markets for everyone who participates. As one of the largest market making institutions, we are a trusted partner of 70+ exchanges across the globe.

What you'll get 

You’ll join a culture of collaboration and excellence, where you’ll be surrounded by curious thinkers and creative problem solvers. Motivated by a passion for continuous improvement, you’ll thrive in a supportive, high-performing environment alongside talented colleagues, working collectively to tackle the toughest problems in the financial markets.

In addition, you’ll receive:

- A performance-based bonus structure, enabling all of our employees to benefit from our global profit pool.

- 27 paid vacation days plus all UK public holidays.

- Daily breakfast and lunch, along with support on commuting expenses.

- Private medical insurance, pension scheme, and ClassPass fitness membership.

- Training and continuous learning opportunities, including access to conferences and tech events.

- International transfer opportunities for global career growth.

How to apply 

Are you interested in furthering your career on one of the most dynamic and exciting trading floors in Europe? 

Apply directly via the form below. If you have any questions feel free to contact our Recruitment team via our recruitment inquiry form .

Please note:

- We do not require any assistance from third-parties including agencies in the recruitment of this role

- We cannot accept applications via email

Optiver is committed to diversity and inclusion .

A distributed storage cluster continuously emits telemetry at every level, from the platform and S3 service down to each server and disk. A failing disk, server or storage node leaves traces in these multivariate time series, from subtle shifts in a few metrics to system-wide disruption. Detecting and diagnosing these anomalies early is critical for:

- Predictive maintenance: isolating or replacing a component before it impacts service

- Faster diagnosis: pointing support engineers to the root cause, not just to an alert

- Higher availability and durability of customer data

This internship is part of a joint research project between Scality and an INRIA research team. The project released SHAD (Scality High-dimensional Anomaly Detection), an open benchmark published at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). It contains 215 real 171-dimensional time series from Scality RING clusters, annotated for injected disk, server and storage-node failures. SHAD's baselines show the problem is far from solved. No detector handles every failure type, per-dimension attributions find root causes no better than chance, and off-the-shelf LLMs cannot interpret the anomalies. This internship builds on SHAD to close these gaps.

More details on the project: scality.github.io/shad 

Your Mission 
As part of our R&D team and in close collaboration with INRIA researchers, you will develop AI models that detect, explain and interpret anomalies in storage-cluster telemetry. Your work will include: 

1. State of the Art

Review the literature and open-source projects on multivariate time series anomaly detection, root-cause attribution and LLM-based interpretation of time series. Also survey recent work on AI agents that automate research and experimentation. Starting points include SHAD and the TSB-AD benchmark. 

2. Anomaly Detection & Diagnosis Models

Design, train and benchmark models that improve on SHAD's baselines at each stage of the pipeline:

- Detection that stays accurate across disk, server and storage-node failures (e.g., ensembles, hybrid models, time series foundation models)

- Explanation: attributing each anomaly to the dimensions that actually cause it

- Interpretation: turning detections into actionable diagnoses (failure type, criticality, affected component) 

- Early detection of progressive degradations, the core of predictive maintenance

3. Fleets of AI Agents for Research

Set up and manage fleets of AI agents that run your studies at scale:

- Design agent workflows that launch experiments, run benchmarks and compare methods

- Orchestrate and monitor many agents working in parallel

- Build safeguards for rigor: experiment tracking, reproducibility, independent verification of results

- Assess what agent-driven research changes in practice: speed, coverage, failure modes

4. Evaluation & Validation

Evaluate every model with rigorous, reproducible protocols. Use them to:

- Measure each stage with SHAD's metrics (VUS-PR for detection, NDCG for explanation, a questionnaire for interpretation)
Quantify performance per failure family and scenario

- Identify which approaches are ready to transfer to production monitoring

Expected Outcomes & Valorization 
Depending on results, the work may be valorized through:

- A scientific publication with the Scality and INRIA researchers

- New methods and baselines contributed to the open-source SHAD benchmark

- Reusable agent-based research workflows for the R&D team

Technical Stack 

- Python (primary language for modeling, experimentation and analysis)

- PyTorch and scikit-learn (deep learning and classical models)

- SHAD benchmark (github.com/scality/shad) and TSB-AD (github.com/TheDatumOrg/TSB-AD) for data, detectors and evaluation

- LLM-based AI agents and their orchestration tooling

Candidate Profile 

- Final-year student in a Master's program or Engineering school (Bac+5), in machine learning, data science or computer science

- Solid foundations in machine learning; experience with time series or anomaly detection is a strong plus

- Strong interest in LLMs and AI agents, and curiosity for new ways of doing research

- Good Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch

- Rigorous and critical with experimental results, especially when agents produce them

- Autonomous and curious, able to communicate results clearly in written and spoken English

- Interest in distributed systems or storage is a plus, not a prerequisite

Work Environment 
You will join a fast-paced, lean AI R&D team. French and English is our primary working language. You will benefit from:

- Mentorship from R&D engineers

- Close collaboration with INRIA researchers working on time series anomaly detection

- Access to real telemetry from Scality RING clusters and to the AI agent tooling the team uses for its studies

- A high-trust environment where your findings will directly influence engineering decisions

Why Join Scality? 

- Work on a concrete research problem with real-world industrial impact

- Build on a benchmark published at NeurIPS and contribute to open research

- Practice a new way of doing research, with fleets of AI agents as research assistants

- Be part of a team building infrastructure trusted by Fortune 500 companies

- Potential to publish research or continue as a full-time engineer after the internship

title: Robotics Application Engineer
description:

We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. Robotics Application Engineer – Rhoda AI GmbH (Germany) 

About Rhoda AI GmbH 
Rhoda AI GmbH is Rhoda AI's first international entity, established to own strategic partner relationships across Europe and drive deployment of Robotics as a Service (RaaS). It's a small, high-ownership team: you'll work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one, with a direct line to our engineering organization in Silicon Valley.

About the Application Engineering Team 
Application Engineering is where Rhoda's AI meets the real world. We work directly with customers and strategic partners to understand their operational problems, determine where our platform can deliver value, and lead the application of Rhoda's AI model end to end — from model post-training and data collection, to robot tooling and work-cell design, to production deployments on the customer's floor. The team sits at the intersection of engineering, product, deployment operations, and business, with members in the US and Germany. Application Engineering is organized into three complementary roles — Application Engineers, Solution Engineers, and Technical Program Managers.

The Role 
As a Robotics Application Engineer, you are a core member of Rhoda AI's European team and the hands-on technical lead in the early stages of a partner engagement — Scoping, Proof of Principle (POP), and Proof of Concept (POC) — through to RaaS deployment. You'll determine whether a use case is feasible, design and prototype the end effectors and task tooling a robot needs to do the job, write the data collection procedures that feed our models, and post-train Rhoda's AI model to perform the task. You'll spend real time on partner sites across Europe standing up POCs and showing what our platform can do.

You'll also serve as a key technical bridge between our European partners and Rhoda HQ Engineering, owning the feedback loop that turns field findings into product improvements.

What You'll Do 

- Scope new partner use cases alongside the commercial team: ask the right questions, assess technical feasibility, and make go/no-go recommendations.

- Design, prototype, and iterate on end effectors and task-specific tooling for real-world manipulation tasks.

- Author and refine data collection SOPs, and work with teleoperation and ML ops teams to gather high-quality training data.

- Post-train and evaluate Rhoda's AI model on partner tasks, driving performance toward POC success criteria.

- Lead on-site POP/POC setup and execution, including model training, daily reporting, validation, and direct partner interaction, and author the final technical report.

- Partner with Solution Engineers on task engineering and solution design input as engagements move toward production.

- Review proposals and provide technical feedback ahead of purchase orders.

- Support model training through Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), deployment, and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT).

- Lead root cause analysis for issues surfaced during deployments, troubleshooting across hardware, firmware, and software until the real cause is found.

- Share field learnings with product and engineering in Silicon Valley, translating partner-reported issues into prioritized, actionable input for the roadmap.

- Present clear, non-technical summaries of technical outcomes to partner leadership, and work with the commercial team to tie them to commercial milestones.

What You'll Bring 

- BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field.

- 3–8 years of hands-on experience in robotics, automation, systems integration, or applied engineering in an industrial setting, including real-world deployments or field installations.

- Strong mechanical design skills, including CAD (e.g., SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion) and rapid prototyping (3D printing, machining, off-the-shelf components).

- Working knowledge of machine learning workflows — data collection, training, and evaluation — and comfort working in Python.

- Experience with robot arms, grippers, and sensors (cameras, depth sensors, LiDAR, IMUs) in real environments, including integration and calibration.

- Proven track record conducting root cause analysis on complex systems spanning hardware, firmware, and software.

- Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working with ambiguity in high-stakes environments.

- Clear communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to partners, executives, and internal teams. Fluent English required; German at working level minimum.

- Willingness to travel approximately 40% across Europe, including extended on-site POC periods, with occasional travel to the US.

Nice to Have 

- Experience with imitation learning, VLA models, world models, or robot foundation models.

- Background in factory automation, material handling, or logistics.

- Experience in a customer-facing technical role (application, field, FDE, or sales engineering) at a robotics OEM, system integrator, or corporate automation department.

- Familiarity with teleoperation systems or remote robot management workflows.

- Experience with ROS/ROS2, embedded Linux, or C/Rust for onboard software.

Why Rhoda AI GmbH 

- Work on real customer problems, not lab demos: our robots are ready for field deployment directly after a successful POC.

- Direct line to HQ Engineering — your field intelligence shapes the product roadmap.

- Small, high-ownership team where you work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one.

title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence
description:
Headquarters: New Jersey, USA

URL: https://vertican.com 

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

- Monthly payments in USD

Vertican is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/vertican-senior-applied-ai-engineer-document-intelligence

title: Financial Crime Compliance, Senior Analyst
description:
Company Description 

We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. 

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. 

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. 

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. 

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. 

Please only apply using an English CV. 

We're hiring for a passionate FinCrime problem solver to join the Financial Crime Compliance team in Paris and help protect the future of real-time payments. 

As a Senior Analyst, you will use your expertise in AML and complex onboarding to solve complex challenges in one of the world’s fastest-growing fintech environments. The Financial Crime Compliance team is the engine ensuring we grow safely. 

Key Responsibilities

- Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD): Lead deep-dive investigations into high-risk corporate entities and complex ownership structures (UBOs).

- SARs/STRs Management: Identify suspicious patterns and draft high-quality Suspicious Activity Reports (Déclarations de Soupçon) for submission to TRACFIN.

- Regulatory Advisory: Act as a subject matter expert on French AML/CFT laws (Monetary and Financial Code) and help the MLRO translate these into scalable operational processes.

- Transaction Monitoring: Analyze real-time alerts and historical data to identify emerging financial crime trends.

- Process Optimization: Don't just follow the manual—help write it. You’ll identify gaps in our automated screening and monitoring tools and propose data-driven solutions.

- Audit & Liaison: Support the MLRO during regulatory onsite inspections or internal audits, providing clear rationales for risk-based decisions.

About you

- Experience: 5+ years in Financial Crime, AML, or Compliance, ideally within a FinTech, Payment Service Provider (PSP), or a high-volume Tier 1 bank.

- Local Expertise: Deep understanding of the French regulatory landscape (ACPR, TRACFIN) and the 5th/6th Anti-Money Laundering Directives.

- The "Investigator" Mindset: You enjoy "following the money" and have a proven ability to synthesize complex data into clear, actionable risk assessments.

- Tech-Savvy: Comfortable working with SQL, Python, or advanced data visualization tools (Looker/Tableau) to hunt for anomalies.

- Communication: Fluent in French and English. You can explain a complex regulatory requirement to a Product Manager just as easily as you can to a Regulator.

Additional Information 

Bring all of you to work 

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com 

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

title: Senior Reinforcement Learning Engineer
description:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 

The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously. 

About the Job 

The autonomy team at Gravis builds autonomous systems for excavators operating in real construction environments. You will build control modules that run on many different machines , across many sites, with different soil conditions. We’re looking for a roboticist with data driven planning and/or control background, deep python expertise and good level of C++ proficiency.

What you will do 

Learning-Based Planning and Control for Real Systems 

- Develop data driven planning and control systems for autonomous excavation that generalize across machine models and soil conditions 

- Contribute to simulation improvements that reduce or address the sim2real gap 

- Define data collection and curation pipelines for incorporating real data in policy training 

- Design experiments focused on continuous performance and robustness improvements. 

- Explore the usage of adaptive and online reinforcement learning in deployed systems 

- Provide mentorship and supervision for junior team members, interns, and students. 

System Integration 

- Integrate learned components into a larger software stack 

- Collaborate with excavation and motion planning engineers 

- Build tools for analysing and evaluating the behavior of learned components 

What we’re looking for 

We recognize that excellent candidates come from diverse backgrounds with various combinations of skills. If you meet most of the core qualifications below, we highly encourage you to apply. 

Core qualifications 

- 
2–5 years industry experience developing Reinforcement learning systems for control and/or planning and deploying them on real robots with a customer. If you only have experience with simulation, you’re most likely not a good fit for this position. 

- 
Experience with GPU accelerated simulation environments (e.g. IsaacSim/IsaacLab, CARLA, MuJoCo) 

- 
Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or similar libraries 

- 
Proficiency in C++ 

- 
Comfortable debugging real-world system behavior 

- 
Ability and willingness to travel as required by business projects. 

Great-to-Have Skills & Experience 

- 
Experience with hydraulic machinery 

- 
Experience with supervised learning or imitation learning 

- 
Research experience in reinforcement learning 

- 
Experience deploying robotic systems at scale (e.g. hundreds of units) 

- 
Familiarity with ROS or similar robotics frameworks 

- 
Experience with feature-flagged deployments, staged rollouts, or long-lived platforms 

- 
Experience with data curation for ML applications 

- 
Experience guiding, mentoring, or leading junior colleagues, students, or project teams. 

- 
Familiarity with or interest in utilizing AI coding tools. 

This Role is a Great Fit If 

- 
You are passionate about building systems that work reliably in the real world 

-

- 
You are comfortable working with the realities of imperfect data and noisy measurements. 

-

title: Member of Technical Staff - Safety
description:
About Black Forest Labs

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We're creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.

Why this role

FLUX models ship as open weights, which gives anyone full access to the model. Our safety efforts focus on suppressing harmful behaviors and mitigating the risk of misuse, so safety has to be built into the models themselves, not bolted on afterwards.

As a Member of Technical Staff on our safety research team, you'll research and ship methods that make FLUX models safe by design: from what goes into the training data to how the models are mid- and post-trained, across images, video and the text that conditions them. This is a role with real ownership: you won't just do research on model safety, you'll shape it. The methods you build ship in FLUX models with over 75 million downloads on Hugging Face and in production at some of the largest platforms in the world.

What you'll work on

- Develop mid- and post-training safety methods for FLUX models, such as safety SFT, preference optimization and RL with safety rewards, and concept erasure.

- Build safety data filtering that runs at pretraining scale: classifiers and pipelines that screen billions of images, video clips and captions, with measured Pareto frontiers and precision/recall trade-offs.

- Make safety hold up for open-weight releases, including robustness to adversarial prompts and to downstream fine-tuning.

- Extend safety to the text side of the stack: prompts, captions and the text encoders that condition our models.

- Design evaluations and red-teaming that measure harmful generations alongside image quality and prompt following, so safety gains don't come at the cost of performance.

- Work directly with pretraining and post-training teams so your methods land in the release model, and publish where it makes sense.

What we're looking for

- Hands-on research experience in visual safety: safety of text-to-image, text-to-video or vision-language models, such as harm classifiers, safe generation methods or safety benchmarks.

- Proven experience in at least one of:

- Large-scale safety data filtering: building and running classifiers or filtering pipelines over hundreds of millions of samples or more.

- Safety mid- or post-training: safety SFT, DPO or RL with safety objectives, or unlearning applied to large generative models.

- Deep familiarity with concept erasure methods (e.g. ESD, UCE, adversarial unlearning) and their failure modes, such as concept recovery and collateral damage to unrelated concepts.

- Track record of shipping: top-venue publications (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV) paired with production impact, or unambiguous production wins at a frontier lab.

- Experience with distributed training at multi-node scale.

- Strong PyTorch fluency; you write research code that others can build on. You work fluently with coding agents to move faster, and have the depth to verify their output and own the result.

- Experience running multi-agent workflows: you know which tasks to hand off and which to keep yourself, and you use the speed-up to raise the quality bar, not lower it.

We'd be especially excited if you:

- Know how to keep safety intact after release, when others fine-tune open weights.

- Have tackled safety for video generation, where harm can emerge across frames rather than in any single frame.

- Bring experience with audio safety, especially for jointly generated audio and video, where each modality can amplify harm in the other.

- Have unlearned concepts from text encoders or built safety-tuned encoders (e.g. Safe-CLIP-style approaches).

- Have worked on text safety: LLM safety tuning, prompt and jailbreak defenses, or text safety classifiers, ideally across languages.

- Have applied latent-space safety methods, such as activation steering or safe guidance.

- Have built VLM-based safety judges or guard models for filtering or evaluation.

How we work together

We're a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You'll join us in Freiburg at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week). We'll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we've structured things to make it accessible to all. We'll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process.

Everything we do is grounded in four values:

- Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

- Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

- Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

- Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

If this sounds like work you'd enjoy, we'd love to hear from you.

Compensation 

EUR 160K-220K + equity, depending on profile

title: Senior AI Engineer
description:
This role may require in-person interview/s. 

About Osano :

Osano is an innovative B-Corporation built around a simple belief: privacy is a fundamental right. Since day one, we’ve been focused on giving modern enterprises the ability to innovate quickly, stay competitive, and earn customer trust by respecting data privacy and complying with consent guidelines. Our products help organizations operate confidently in a rapidly evolving regulatory and technological landscape.

About the Role: 

We’re hiring a Senior AI Engineer to build and improve Osano AI, our intelligent privacy assistant. As part of the Osano AI team, you will take capabilities from first idea to production, with an emphasis on delivering capabilities that are reliable, measurable, and trustworthy.

This role goes beyond wrapping APIs or building chat interfaces. We are looking for an engineer who has shipped LLM-powered systems that real users depend on. That means that you’ve dealt with hallucinations, latency, cost, evaluation, and tricky edge cases within agentic systems, and you know what it takes to keep these non-deterministic systems working after launch.

You will often work on problems that aren’t well-defined. Success here depends on how you think, communicate, and work with others as much as on what you build. This position is ideal for someone who is highly technical, thrives in ambiguity, takes ownership of 0→1 initiatives, wants to have an outsized impact, and believes responsible AI is non-negotiable.

Responsibilities:

Build and ship production AI 

- Design, build, and maintain agentic features across our products, from early prototype to scaled production deployments.

- Build retrieval (RAG) systems that build trust through verifiable sources.

- Build agentic and multi-step workflows with guardrails, observability, and structured outputs.

- Balance quality, latency, reliability, and cost in production.

Measure and improve AI systems 

- Build thorough evaluation frameworks that cover accuracy, grounding, latency, and reliability, utilizing both offline evaluations and real-world production signals.

- Deploy data-driven methods to decide what to ship, how to fix it, and what to stop doing.

- Continuously refine deployed systems based on measurable outcomes.

Collaborate and communicate 

- Work closely with product managers, engineers, privacy experts, and other stakeholders to decide what to build, how to build it, and why.

- Write clear design documents and run effective technical discussions.

Privacy-First Development 

- Embed privacy-by-design principles across the AI stack.

- Ensure compliance, data sovereignty, and secure handling practices.

- Collaborate cross-functionally to align AI capabilities with regulatory standards.

About You: 

- You’re curious, self-directed, and motivated to learn quickly.

- You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and creating clarity for others.

- You’re excited about privacy, responsible AI, and building trustworthy technology.

- You are willing to relentlessly pursue the best, most responsible ways to leverage AI—without overselling its capabilities or ignoring its limitations.

Must-Haves: 

- 5+ years of professional software engineering or AI/ML experience

- Demonstrated experience building and running agentic systems in production with real users, not just prototypes or internal demos.

- Deep technical understanding of LLM usage and orchestration beyond prompt engineering.

- Proven experience building complex RAG systems and autonomous AI agents.

- Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain technical trade-offs to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.

- Concrete examples of getting from ambiguity to results.

Nice-to-Haves: 

- Strong expertise in the Python AI ecosystem, including FastAPI and LangGraph.

- Experience with Knowledge Graphs to enhance RAG precision

- Familiarity with Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs)

- Experience with data anonymization techniques

- Background in compliance-heavy or regulated environments

Why Us: 

- We're a welcoming team that's dependable, curious, moves fast, and full of talented people

- We're a B-corporation with a mission that matters, in a high-growth space with significant potential

- You'll have access to our training program, well-defined career paths, and a leadership team that values professional development

Benefits: 

- Competitive-pay compensation and ownership interest/equity

- Unlimited paid time off, plus a requirement to take at least two weeks off per year

- We're a Best Place for Working Parents and offer paid parental leave for all new parents

- Osano sponsors individual premiums on base plans at 100% and dependent premiums at 50% for Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance via Aetna

- A fully and permanently remote company, so you can work from anywhere in the U.S.

- Receive a MacBook and $600 to craft your home workspace

- Annual company trip designed to foster connection, creativity, and fun

- Mental health benefits with free memberships to mindfulness and talk therapy services

A Bit More About Osano 

Osano is a leading data privacy platform that helps organizations quickly and confidently comply with laws like GDPR, CCPA, and other global privacy regulations. From consent management to vendor risk monitoring, Osano makes complex privacy tasks refreshingly simple, so companies can focus on what they do best, while we handle the rest.

We’re backed by top-tier investors including Baird Capital, Jump Capital, and LiveOak, and we’re scaling fast with a multi-year runway and ambitious growth plans. We’ve also been recognized as a Great Place to Work for four years running, with 97% of employees saying Osano is a great place to work.

As we grow, we're looking for individuals who lean into modern technologies and smarter systems to drive efficiency, clarity, and speed; both in our product and in how we operate. If you're excited by the idea of helping build a high-growth, privacy-first company that embraces thoughtful automation, emerging tech, and intentional collaboration, we’d love to hear from you.

Osano is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Spacecraft Thermal Engineer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.

We are seeking a Spacecraft Thermal Engineer to join our Thermal Control System team. You will contribute to the preparation, execution and analysis of thermal verification activities, including Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) and Thermal Balance testing, and support spacecraft assembly, integration and test. Alongside these activities, you will take technical ownership of assigned thermal control products, following their development, supplier activities, qualification and delivery for integration.

You will work closely with AIT, suppliers, external test facilities and other subsystem teams. You will be part of the TCS & ECLSS Team and report to the Principal Thermal Control System Engineer.

Key Responsibilities:

Product Ownership and Supplier Follow-up

- Take technical ownership of assigned thermal control products, from requirements and interface definition through qualification and delivery for integration, with guidance from senior engineers.

- Act as the day-to-day technical interface with suppliers, following design, manufacturing, testing and delivery activities.

- Review supplier deliverables, including design justifications, test procedures and reports, against agreed requirements.

- Maintain product requirements, interfaces, configuration information and technical documentation.

- Prepare product review documentation and coordinate the closure of review actions.

- Track product maturity, technical risks and delivery milestones, escalating issues affecting performance, cost or schedule.

- Coordinate with AIT to ensure hardware is delivered with the appropriate configuration, documentation and verification status.

Thermal Testing and Verification

- Contribute to the definition of thermal test objectives, configurations and success criteria.

- Prepare test plans, procedures and instrumentation requirements in coordination with AIT and test facilities.

- Support spacecraft-level TVAC and Thermal Balance campaigns, and coordinate testing activities for assigned thermal control products.

- Contribute to test readiness reviews, test execution and anomaly investigations.

- Prepare test reports and verification evidence, maintaining traceability to applicable requirements.

- Track verification activities and follow technical actions through to closure within your assigned scope.

Flight Model Integration and AIT Support

- Work alongside AIT teams during the installation, integration and verification of thermal control hardware.

- Contribute to integration procedures, thermal instrumentation layouts and test configurations.

- Support functional testing, troubleshooting and spacecraft system check-outs.

- Support leak testing and fluid loop commissioning, as applicable to assigned activities.

- Investigate integration issues with the relevant engineering, supplier and quality teams.

Thermal Test Data Analysis

- Support pre-test thermal predictions in collaboration with thermal analysts.

- Process and analyse test data to assess hardware and system performance against requirements.

- Contribute to thermal model correlation and the investigation of discrepancies between predictions and test results.

- Recommend design or test improvements and capture lessons learned.

What We Would Love to See from You

Qualifications:

- Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Thermodynamics or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

- 3+ years of relevant experience in spacecraft thermal engineering, including thermal hardware development, integration or testing.

- Hands-on experience contributing to thermal test campaigns, such as TVAC or Thermal Balance testing.

- Good understanding of spacecraft thermal control hardware, such as MLI, temperature sensors, heaters and fluid loop components.

- Familiarity with spacecraft qualification and acceptance processes, requirements traceability and verification documentation.

- Experience contributing to hardware development or supplier follow-up, including reviewing technical documentation and tracking actions.

- Familiarity with thermal instrumentation, data acquisition systems and test facility interfaces.

- Experience processing and analysing engineering data using Python, MATLAB or equivalent tools.

- Familiarity with applicable space engineering standards, including ECSS and NASA ones.

- Fluent in English. German, French and Italian are an asset.

Skills and Behaviors:

- Ownership mindset, with the ability to drive assigned activities to completion and seek support when needed.

- Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills.

- Clear written and verbal communication.

- Ability to organise priorities, maintain technical documentation and follow actions through to closure.

- Collaborative approach to working across engineering disciplines, suppliers and AIT teams.

- Positive and flexible attitude to getting the job done.

- Behaviours consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Vision, Competence, Integrity and Passion.

Why you should join us! 

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: 

- We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

- We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them 

- We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge? 

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. 

The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable. 

All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. If applicable, you will receive an email from Zinc upon acceptance of your offer with a link to a secure portal where you can provide the required information to Zinc.

At Schuberg Philis, the world is shifting from traditional backup to data security and resilience. We’re looking for a Platform Engineer to strengthen our Data Management-as-a-Service (DMS) team and help us build the next generation of our platform.

About the Team

The DMS team builds and runs a shared, fully segregated data resilience platform that serves more than 20 of our customers. Customer teams consume it through self-service, and they handle their own day-to-day backup and restore operations. That means you won’t spend your days on job monitoring, restore tickets or backup schedules. Your customers are internal and external engineering teams, and your product is the platform they build on.

You’ll join a dedicated group of data security experts within our larger Services Team and work closely with our sbp.cloud team, who operate our self-built sovereign cloud solutions. With our plan-build-run approach, you take end-to-end ownership: you design it, you build it, you run it.

The Challenge

Running one platform for 20+ customers means solving the hard problems of platform engineering:

- Multi-tenancy by design: strict isolation of data, access, and performance between customers, on shared infrastructure.

title: Principal Software Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
The role 

Reporting directly to the VP Technology, you'll build new capability for Awin with AI at the core, free from the constraints of our established delivery model. You'll take ideas from concept to production quickly, prove what works, and turn the best of it into patterns the wider engineering organisation can adopt.

You'll work closely with product and commercial leaders to find where AI changes the economics of our affiliate marketing platform: what we can build, how fast, and at what cost. You'll be hands-on most of the time, writing code, shipping and measuring results, rather than coordinating others.

You'll know enough of our existing platform to connect new things to it safely, but you won't be absorbed into running it. Your job is to show what modern, AI-native engineering looks like at Awin, and make it real.

This is a step-up opportunity. We're looking for a bright, self-starting engineer who is ready for more scope than their current role allows. You might not have held a principal title yet. What matters is that you're already building this way, you learn fast, and you want the room to prove it. You'll have direct access to senior leadership, real problems with commercial weight, and the freedom to choose how you solve them.

Key tasks and accountabilities 

Build and ship 

- Design, build and run AI-powered products, tools and services from prototype to production

- Own outcomes end to end: problem framing, architecture, implementation, evaluation, release and operation

- Run fast, time-boxed experiments; scale what works and stop what doesn't, with the evidence to back either call

- Set up and evolve the AI infrastructure these builds rely on: model access, evaluation tooling, observability and guardrails

Shape direction 

- Work with the VP Technology to set Awin's engineering-specific AI direction, grounded in what has actually been built and measured

- Scope strategic opportunities early with product and commercial leaders, with effort, cost and value made explicit

- Make clear recommendations on build vs buy, model and vendor choice, and where AI should not be used

Architecture and design 

- Design new capability so it connects safely to the existing platform: APIs, events, data and identity

- Select tools and technologies, and define the patterns and practices for AI-native development at Awin

- Weigh long-term maintainability, economic viability and reuse against speed, and document the trade-offs

Spread what works 

- Turn proven builds into reusable patterns, templates and internal tools, and share them so other teams can adopt them without hand-holding

Ways of working 

- Works autonomously, guided by the VP Technology's priorities rather than team-level delivery processes

- Engages directly with engineering, product, data, security and commercial stakeholders as each build requires

Skills & Expertise 

AI-native engineering 

- Builds with coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) as the default way of working. Can show how they decompose work, manage context and review agent output to get production-quality code at pace

- Has shipped LLM-powered features to production: prompt and context engineering, tool use and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval (RAG) and multi-step agent workflows

- Builds evaluations first: test sets, automated evals and regression checks for non-deterministic behaviour, with quality measured before and after release

- Connects models to enterprise systems and data safely, e.g. MCP servers, internal APIs and event streams, with clear permissions and audit trails

- Understands model selection, token economics, latency, caching and fallback strategies, and can explain cost and benefit trade-offs to commercial stakeholders

- Designs for AI-specific security and privacy risks: prompt injection, data leakage, PII handling under GDPR, and guardrails on what models can do

Engineering foundations 

- Expert in at least one modern language (Python or TypeScript ideal), and able to work in our existing Java, PHP and JavaScript estate when integrating

- Strong cloud-native and serverless architecture on AWS, with infrastructure as code (Terraform)

- Experience with event-driven and distributed systems (Kafka/MSK, SQS/SNS) and with relational and non-relational data stores

- Builds observability into everything: tracing, logging and monitoring, including LLM-specific telemetry

- Treats automated testing, CI/CD and secure-by-default design as standard, and automates as much of the delivery loop as possible

Ways of building 

- Takes an idea to a working prototype in days, then hardens it for production, and knows when to stop

- Leaves behind reusable patterns, templates and internal tools, not one-off solutions

Soft skills 

- Bias to action: ships, measures and iterates rather than waiting for perfect requirements

- Comfortable with ambiguity: frames vague opportunities into concrete, testable bets

- Commercially minded: connects technical choices to revenue, cost and customer outcomes, and balances effort against value

- Intellectually honest: kills their own ideas when the evidence says so, and says plainly where AI is not the answer

- Clear communicator: explains technical trade-offs to executives, engineers and commercial teams in language each understands, in writing and in person

- Influences without authority: gets teams to adopt new patterns because they work, not because they're mandated

Our Offer 

- 
Flexi-Week : We prioritise your mental health and wellbeing by offering you a four-day Flexi-Week (with one lighter or completely disconnected day per week) at full pay, with no reduction to your annual holiday allowance.

- 
Flexi-office : We offer an international culture and flexibility through our hybrid/remote working scheme which is designed to foster a culture of mutual trust and working flexibility.

- 
Work Expense Contribution & Remote Working Furniture : You will receive a monthly allowance to cover part of your running costs, as well as a furniture package to support you in setting up a comfortable workspace when working from home.

- 
Health and Wellbeing : With our support and access to various initiatives and sports offers, you can focus on your mental and physical wellbeing.

- 
Development : We’ve built our extensive training suite, Awin Academy, to cover a wide range of skills that support your professional and personal growth, with trainings conveniently packaged to help your overall development.

- 
Appreciation : Thank and reward colleagues by sending them a voucher through our peer-to-peer recognition programme.

We are hiring in multiple countries for this role. Additional benefits, including health and wellbeing offerings, will be discussed during the initial interview. 

Established in 2000, Awin is proud of our dynamic, social and inclusive culture.

Like all businesses, we’ve had to adapt and nurture our culture in a virtual environment. Our virtual ‘Life @ Awin’ hub brings our colleagues from across the globe together for various social activities.

Diversity & Inclusion are paramount to us, and we proudly pursue and hire diverse team members. We champion uniqueness and authenticity; this is who we are at our core. Our network of affiliate partnerships are diverse and transparent, as are the employees powering our vision to build the world’s leading open partner ecosystem. We welcome all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. If you need support at any point in the application or interview process, please let us know.

Awin is part of the Axel Springer group. Learn more at axelspringer.com/ en / , and explore the Axel Springer Essentials here: axelspringer.com/en/inside/the-essentials-what-we-have-adapted-and-why 

Apply now to begin the next stage of your career at a progressive company that supports both your professional and personal development.

Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. - Design and implement algorithms for 3D object tracking, segmentation, and motion recognition on embedded hardware.

- Help bring ML, computer vision, or signal-processing systems into production with tight performance constraints 

- Build reliable application features and services that customers use in real environments. 

- Analyze production data to find system limits, product issues, and opportunities for improvement. 

- Collaborate closely with the embedded platform team on model optimization and inference performance, and with the applications team on how tracking data becomes product features. 

WHAT YOU’LL NEED 

- 4+ years of software engineering experience in production systems. 

- Strong skill in Python and backend engineering. 

- Working knowledge of C++ or a strong reason to be effective in performance-critical code. 

- Experience with data-intensive systems, distributed systems, parallel processing, or efficient data pipelines. 

- Exposure to ML, ML infrastructure, signal processing, real-time systems, computer vision, or related applied technical areas. 

- A track record of shipping reliable software, not only prototypes. 

- Strong debugging skills and the ability to find the root cause of complex system behavior. 

- Clear communication and good judgment when tradeoffs are not simple. 

- Curiosity, adaptability, and the desire to learn new technical areas. 

Nice to have — and what would make you exceptional:

- Experience with ML model deployment, feature pipelines, evaluation systems, or data quality tools.

- Experience with streaming data, event systems, real-time processing, or low-latency applications.

- Experience with numerical methods, signal processing, filtering, state estimation, or robotics.

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE 

- In 6 months time, you understand the main systems, ship reliable changes, and help improve a meaningful data or product workflow. You give valuable technical input towards solving problems across backend, data, and perception systems.

- In 12 months time, you have made a measurable impact on system reliability, product capability, or data quality. You own important parts of the architecture and help the team make better technical decisions.

WHY CATAPULT? 

- We have amazing people. We promise you’ll work with some of the most ambitious, intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.

- We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary.

- Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.

That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve. There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

title: Senior Optical Design Engineer
description:
Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life.

Overview

We are expanding our optomechanical capabilities, and the success of our projects depends on optical designs that are precise, manufacturable, and verified through rigorous analysis and testing. As a Senior Optical Design Engineer, you will own optical designs from concept through lab validation, turning requirements into lens designs and optical assemblies that perform reliably in the real world. This position is central to our mission of delivering cutting-edge free-space optical systems for space applications, and it will support successful pre-production runs and strong collaboration with our suppliers. This position reports to our Responsible Engineer, Optical Systems, and is based in our Toulouse, France office. Our working language is English. 

What you will be doing 

- 
Design and optimize lenses and optical systems, from first-order layout to detailed optimization with ray tracing and physical optics propagation (POP). 

- 
Carry out tolerance analysis and Monte Carlo simulations to predict manufacturing and assembly yield, and define realistic tolerances with suppliers. 

- 
Conduct STOP (Structural-Thermal-Optical Performance) analysis with mechanical engineers, verifying performance and margins across operating conditions. 

- 
Conduct stray light analysis. 

- 
Produce lens and optomechanical drawings, and work with mechanical engineers to ensure designs are manufacturable and assemblable. 

- 
Define assembly, alignment, and bonding procedures, and support their implementation in clean room environments. 

- 
Plan and execute lab assembly and test, covering alignment, characterization, and performance verification of prototypes and flight-representative hardware. 

- 
Characterize components and assemblies through optical metrology, and identify discrepancies . D rive root-cause investigations and design iterations. 

- 
Work with suppliers on design for manufacturing, tolerancing, inspection, qualification, and pre-production runs. 

What you bring to this role 

- 
A Master’s degree in Optical Engineering, Physics, or a related field, with a strong foundation in geometrical and physical optics. 

- 
5+ years of experience in optical design, including lens and optical system design , optimization and STOP analysis. 

- 
Proficiency in Zemax OpticStudio, including sequential ray tracing and optimization. 

- 
Hands-on lab experience in optical assembly and test, with working knowledge of metrology instruments such as interferometers, wavefront sensors, MTF benches, autocollimators, and centration measurement tools. 

- 
Experience with spaceborne optics or qualification to space-relevant standards, such as ECSS. Selection of adhesives, coatings and optics materials. 

- 
Strong analytical skills and the ability to troubleshoot problems across simulation and hardware. 

- 
A proactive mindset and a commitment to high standards of quality and performance. 

Bonus points 

- 
Experience with free space optical communication systems . 

- 
Python and ZOS-API skills for automating analysis or processing data. 

- 
Experience with ANOVA methodology, including Gauge R&R studies and statistical post-processing in tools such as JMP. 

- 
Practical knowledge of cleanroom practice, optics cleaning, adhesive bonding .

Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow, with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.

With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

As a Senior Engineer, you'll be at the forefront of developing financial products that will shape the future of how businesses manage their finances. Along with expanding into new markets and handling an increasing volume of transactions, Mollie has recently introduced exciting new products to broaden our offering. You’ll have the opportunity to bring your ideas to life and contribute to these impactful projects. Mollie Capital offers easy access to flexible financing, providing funding to support growth and cash flow management. In-person payments , allows merchants to accept payments at their physical stores through our terminal and mobile app. These innovations are just the beginning, enabling Mollie to offer a seamless, all-in-one payment solution and money management platform.

What You will Be Doing: 

- Building Large-Scale Systems: Designing and engineering systems that can scale to handle high volumes of transactions.

- Developing Products Our Customers Love: Iterating from an idea to the final solution, shaping, building, testing, and measuring the performance of the features our customers love.

- Mentorship: Providing guidance and support to junior team members, fostering their growth through mentoring, knowledge-sharing, and hands-on collaboration.

- Tech Leadership: Leading technical initiatives from architecture design to implementation, ensuring engineering excellence.

- Problem-Solving: Utilising your creative problem-solving skills and analytical abilities to resolve complex issues and contribute to our mission of making financial processes effortless.

- Documentation and Knowledge Sharing : Creating comprehensive documentation to facilitate domain knowledge sharing and set up optimised processes.

- Engineering Excellence: Owning the code quality and engineering excellence and best practices of our systems.

What You’ll Bring: 

- Always Be Shipping Mindset: It’s about consistently delivering value to customers, where speed and quality go hand in hand.

- 6+ years of experience in developing large-scale applications, preferably with PHP or Java. Experience with Go, C#, or Python is also valued but you are willing to work with PHP or Java.

- Proven experience in leading architectural decisions and technical initiatives, delivering end-to-end solutions, and optimising processes.

- Experience in mentoring junior developers and implementing strategies to drive team growth and skill development.

- Excellent communication skills, with experience working effectively with various stakeholders. Can explain complex problems and solutions in simple terms.

- Creative problem-solving skills and the ability to shape ideas with a product-first approach, as well as analyse and resolve complex issues.

- Ability to hold yourself accountable for your tasks, and show a willingness to proactively identify and improve things, whether technical or business related.
